display.purpose: Cinzel 40/600 for the balance numeral at dial center; tabular-nums, gold (coral --danger when overspent). One of only two Cinzel sites.

wordmark.purpose: Cinzel 600, 0.18em tracked uppercase GILD — 16px in the top bar, 22px in the drawer head. The other Cinzel site.

engraved.purpose: 10px/600, 0.24em tracked uppercase in ink-3 — dial-print grammar (LEFT TO SPEND). Labels instruments, never prose sections.

section-title.purpose: Hanken Grotesk 15/700, -0.01em, sentence case, full ink — prose region headings.

body.purpose: Hanken Grotesk 14/500 for category names and row titles; drawer items 16/500; figures 600–700 with tabular-nums.

caption.purpose: 12–13px/500 tabular captions: dial subline, subdial figures, category spent/budget.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Cards: soft dark lift plus a faint top-edge catch of light.

shadows.name: row-lift
shadows.purpose: Category rows; subdials use the same throw at 0.25 alpha.

shadows.name: inset-only
shadows.purpose: Tiles, secondary buttons, list rows, segmented controls: seated flat.

shadows.name: drawer-throw
shadows.purpose: The slide-in drawer over a rgba(4,8,6,0.6) scrim.

motion.name: drawer-in
motion.purpose: Drawer slide-in (translateX -40px + fade) with a 0.25s ease-out scrim fade. The shared decelerate curve.

motion.name: press-compress
motion.purpose: Primary button press. The dial itself is still — a watch face, not an animation.

narrative.overview: Gild is haute horlogerie, not fintech. The ground is dial black, text is chalk ink, and one champagne gold plays the role of applied metal — granted to exactly four things: the balance numeral, the remaining day ticks/arcs, the one primary action, and the active selection state. The pay period is a power reserve rendered as a 296px dial: one tick per day, spent days faint, remaining days gold, today long and bright, with the money left set at center in Cinzel gold above a days-left · per-day subline in engraved-caps dial print. Budgets are complications — chronograph subdial arcs capped at 100%, because a gauge never lies past its stops. Money movement is muted sage in, warm bronze out; coral appears only for genuinely over budget, in two calibrated shades (large/graphic vs. small text). Two faces divide strictly: Cinzel for the balance and wordmark only, Hanken Grotesk for everything else. Radial composition belongs to the instrument alone; below it the page returns to refined left-reading rows. Depth is hairlines and soft dark shadows on flat plates — no blur, no gradients, no blobs — and the only decorated surface in the world is the guilloché engine-turning inside the dial itself. This world refuses the fintech card stack, the editorial serif ledger, and the green-banking calm that preceded it; both prior worlds are dead and none of their rules apply. Only the Dashboard and the shared chrome are fully realized; Bills, Transactions, and Balances have had a money/date formatting pass, and the remaining screens inherit the tokens through back-compat aliases without a dedicated pass.
keyCharacteristics: Dial black ground (#0E0F12), cool near-black plates, chalk ink — never pure black.
The Gold Grant: champagne gold only on the balance numeral, remaining ticks/arcs, the primary action, and the active place.
Two faces: Cinzel exclusively for the balance numeral and wordmark; Hanken Grotesk (400–800) for all UI.
Data as honest instruments: per-day dial ticks and subdial arcs capped at 100%.
Sage = money in, bronze = money out; two corals (--danger large, --danger-text small) only for genuinely over.

rules.name: The Gold Grant
rules.body: Gold is granted to exactly four things: the balance numeral, the remaining day ticks/arcs, the one primary action per surface, and the active selection state (drawer item, chip, focus ring). Anything else asking for gold is refused.

rules.name: The Complication Rule
rules.body: Data renders as honest instruments: one tick per day of the period, arcs capped at 100%. A gauge never lies past its stops — the numeral states the truth when a budget is exceeded.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Cinzel appears in exactly two places: the balance numeral and the GILD wordmark. Everything else is Hanken Grotesk, with weight carrying hierarchy. A third Cinzel sighting is wrong.

rules.name: The Engraved Caps Rule
rules.body: Instrument labels are engraved caps — 10px/600 at 0.24em tracked uppercase in ink-3, the dial-print grammar. They caption instruments only; prose region headings stay sentence-case at 15/700.

rules.name: The Two-Coral Rule
rules.body: --danger (#C75546) is for large numerals, arcs, and fills; --danger-text (#DB7264) holds 4.5:1 for small text. Both mean genuinely over budget and nothing else.

rules.name: The In/Out Rule
rules.body: Sage always means money in, bronze always means money out; never swap them, and never use coral for ordinary spending.

rules.name: The Radial Instrument Rule
rules.body: Centering belongs to the dial, its pills, and its subdials — the instrument cluster. Everything below returns to left-reading rows; prose and headings are never centered.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no gradients, no blobs. Depth is a hairline and a soft dark shadow; texture is permitted only as the guilloché inside the dial.

dos: Do grant gold only to the balance numeral, remaining ticks/arcs, the primary action, and the active place.
Do render data as instruments: one tick per day, arcs capped at 100%, the numeral stating the truth.
Do keep Cinzel to the balance and wordmark; set everything else in Hanken Grotesk with tabular-nums on money.
Do label instruments in engraved caps and prose regions in sentence case.
Do use --danger for large/graphic coral and --danger-text for small coral text, both only for genuinely over.
Do treat the Dashboard as the canonical reference when passing an inherited screen.
donts: Don't put Cinzel anywhere but the balance numeral and the wordmark.
Don't add gold outside the four granted roles, or let a spent day tick go gold.
Don't draw an arc or fill past its gauge, and don't use --danger at small text sizes.
Don't use coral for ordinary spending or swap the sage/bronze mapping.
Don't reintroduce blur, gradients, or blobs; the glass tokens are aliases only.
Don't resurrect the dead worlds: no green plates, no editorial ledger serif, no burn-down bar.
